column1: # leak-patterns.local.example.tsv — the VALUE LAYER template.
# Copy this OUTSIDE the repository and fill in your real identifiers:
#     mkdir -p ~/.config/leak
#     cp scripts/leak-patterns.local.example.tsv ~/.config/leak/patterns.tsv
#     $EDITOR ~/.config/leak/patterns.tsv
#     ./scripts/leak-scan.sh .
# The gate finds ~/.config/leak/patterns.tsv automatically. Point it elsewhere with
# `--patterns-extra FILE` or $LEAK_PATTERNS_EXTRA.
# DO NOT copy this file into the repository, and do not commit a filled-in copy. The gate refuses
# to run with the value layer inside the tree: `find` enumerates it, its own patterns match its own
# text, and both ways out of that (ignoring it, or widening the self-exclusion) are evasion
# surfaces. Naming your identifiers in a tracked file is the leak this layer exists to prevent.
# Format: NAME<TAB>REGEX. Values are PCRE, so escape metacharacters — a name containing `.` or `+`
# must be written `\.` or `\+`, or it will match more than you meant. A literal tab cannot appear
# in a value, because the tab is the field separator; the gate rejects a malformed line outright
# rather than guessing at what was meant.
# The verdict reports how many of these are applied, and says NOT-CONFIGURED when this file is
# absent. Both states are legitimate. What is not legitimate is a PASS being read as identity
# coverage when the layer never ran.
# NOTE the <YOUR_...> tokens above. They are deliberate and they are load-bearing: the gate treats
# an entry still containing one as INERT and says so, so copying this file without editing it is
# reported as `CONFIGURED BUT INERT` rather than passing as coverage. If you rewrite an entry,
# delete the token — and do not replace it with prose like `Firstname|Lastname`, which the detector
# cannot tell apart from a real value.
# Your name(s), as they would appear in prose, in a path, or on a git author line. This is the one
# risk shape patterns cannot cover, which is why the layer exists at all.
identity-name
# Your GitHub handle. Allowed in hand-written scaffolding (README / ONBOARDING / CONTRIBUTING /
# LICENSE / .github/**), because the repo legitimately points at you there; flagged anywhere inside
# skills/** or Profile/**.
owner-handle
# Optional, and only if the repository is named something you must not publish. If the repo will be
# public under its own name, leave this out — a public repo's own name is not a secret.
#repo-name
